title: The guard refused `git worktree add` for a lane's test-author; judge whether it is a false alarm
why: Lane bg-tail-loses-verdict, 12:37 CST Nov 13: the guard refused `git worktree add`, so the red run ran on a git archive export of main fccff95e6.
note: Todo, possible false alarm (verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent). Lanes run in their own worktree (rule parallelism-own-lane-orchestrator); a worktree add from the lane should be allowed. Read the guard record first; the lane supplies the exact refusal text. Unconfirmed until read. Stood pick on page item 740: an export is acceptable red proof meanwhile. Exact refusals, 12:39 CST Nov 13 (lane bg-tail-loses-verdict, relayed from its test-author). Refusal 1: `git worktree add --detach <shared .claude/worktrees/agent-...-red> fccff95e6` from the agent's own worktree: "a worktree-isolated agent's git operations must target its own worktree". Refusal 2, same command with a scratchpad path: hook hand-made-worktree: a worktree comes only from the Agent tool's isolation option or EnterWorktree; if the tree is your own red-run checkout, write its path out in full; if isolation was refused, make no tree by hand: stop and report to the owner. The path was written in full, so the guard seems to allow the act: a possible false alarm. The test-author then ran the red run on a git archive export after refusal 2 said to stop. That went around the refusal. A one-act override does not reach an agent's call.
